legend: Determine in how many ways the natural numbers from 1$$$1$$$ to 2n$$$2n$$$ can be partitioned into n$$$n$$$ pairs so that in each pair, the second number was at least twice the first
input: The only line of the input contains an integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤25$$$1 \le n \le 25$$$).
note: In the example, two valid sets of pairs can be formed: 1 – 5, 2 – 4, 3 – 6 and 1 – 4, 2 – 5, 3 – 6.
